note.backdrop: Before Friday's open the S&P 500 fund is -0.9%, the Nasdaq 100 fund -1.7%, the Russell 2000 fund -0.4%, S&P 500 futures -0.9% and the VIX +7.7% (the check, 13:34Z); Yahoo's page at about 13:36Z showed the VIX at 30.87 and the 10-year yield at 4.98%. Overnight the AI chip selloff ran through Asia: Taiwan's Taiex -6.2% to 36,033.29, -17.5% for the week, its worst week since 1991 (Bloomberg, via 24/7 Wall St); the KOSPI -5.2% and the Nikkei 225 -5.1%, a seven-month low; SoftBank -14.5% (24/7 Wall St). Treasuries were bought: the 10-year yield fell 6 basis points to 4.989% (CNBC, via StockTitan). Anthropic was $87.92 at 8:02 a.m. ET, 9.52% below Thursday's $97.17 close and 5.9% above its $83 offer price (StockTitan). The check flagged no market-wide move beyond what the market line shows. Today decides whether the S&P 500 has a seventh loss in a row. Four of this morning's eight flags rest on one or two pre-market trades and no news (SAIC, Marqeta, Richardson Electronics, BeOne): the known stray-print flaw, listed as unexplained.

read.says: Chip stocks fell in Asia, Europe and US pre-market trading on Nov 20: AMD -6.31%, TSMC -5.77%, Micron -4.99%, Nvidia -3.26% at $141.23 by 8:02 a.m. ET; Anthropic $87.92, above its $83 offer price; the 10-year yield down 6 bp to 4.989% (CNBC); BJ's EPS included a credit-card fee settlement that cut costs by about $240 million.
Taiwan's Taiex fell 6.2% on Nov 20 and 17.5% for the week, its worst week since 1991 (Bloomberg); KOSPI -5.2%, Nikkei -5.1%; SoftBank -14.5%; Tokyo is shut Monday.
Savara: the FDA will not meet the Nov 22, 2026 PDUFA date for its molgramostim BLA in autoimmune PAP; the review continues and no revised action date has been given.

singles.beneath: The stock had risen into the date (+5.7% Wednesday, +12.8% Thursday), so this gives back the run-up and more. Its cash and equivalents were $29.8 million at Sep 30 against $152.7 million of losses over four quarters, about 0.8 quarters (investments not counted). Before the news the mosaic put the chance of a share-sale filing in 20 sessions at 7.4% against 0.9% for the usual stock. My inference: a delay with no date makes paying for the wait more pressing; that chance is a chance a filing comes, not a direction.
singles.cause: Savara is -25.5%: the FDA will not meet the Nov 22 action date for its lead drug, molgramostim, in autoimmune PAP; the review continues and no new date has been given (its release).

singles.beneath: The last note asked whether application software would follow. So far it has not: Intuit's closest partners over the year are down under 2% (Workday -0.8%, Adobe -0.7%, Salesforce -0.6%, ServiceNow -1.9%) and the software industry median is -1.2%. The fall is about Intuit's own growth, not a repricing of its group.
singles.cause: Intuit is -9.6% before the open, after cutting its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to $23.08-23.37 billion (8% to 9% growth) and drawing several price-target cuts (Stocktwits), and agreeing to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons (its 8-K).

themes.beneath: In proportion: Nvidia at $140.41 (13:36Z) is 13.80% below its $162.89 close of Nov 13; AMD at $454.00 is 14.80% below $532.84; Dell at $292.70 is 14.66% below $342.98. All three are past the desk's size lines (7.5%, 9%, 9.5%), which are judged at today's close. Taiwan's index is mostly technology, so a chip selloff is an index selloff there. My inference: the US-listed Asian funds closed Thursday before Friday's Asian losses (24/7 Wall St), so part of this morning's fall in US chips is that catch-up, and the rest is the week's run of selling.
themes.cause: Asia's chip-heavy markets fell over 5% each on Friday: the Taiex -6.2% (-17.5% for the week), the KOSPI -5.2%, the Nikkei -5.1%; SoftBank -14.5%, Advantest -10.3%, Tokyo Electron -7.1% (24/7 Wall St). ASML fell 5.8% in Europe (CNBC, via StockTitan). Before the US open: AMD -6.3%, TSMC -5.8%, Micron -5.0%, Nvidia -3.3% (StockTitan, 8:01-8:02 a.m. ET); the check's semiconductor industry median is -3.6% over 59 stocks.
themes.mechanism: The same AI-spending worry that sold US chips on Thursday was priced in Asia's Friday session and comes back to US chips at the open. CNBC wrote that markets 'question whether massive investments in AI infrastructure will generate sufficient returns' and that Anthropic's debut 'failed to boost the artificial intelligence trade' (via StockTitan): a view, not a fact.
themes.name: The AI chip selloff went round the world overnight and is back in US chips
themes.watch: Whether US chips close below their pre-market prices (a seventh S&P 500 loss) or recover as Deutsche Bank's 'very oversold' reading would have it (CNBC, an opinion); the three size calls at today's close.

themes.beneath: My inference: when a fall is broad, holders sell what is still up to cover losses elsewhere, and gold had been a winner. Safety buying went to Treasuries, not gold. No source states this; it is a pattern, not a finding.
themes.cause: Gold is -3.4% since Thursday's close, about twice its usual day (1.8%); the metal-mining median is -3.1% (9 stocks), and the stocks most tied to gold fell about as far as their rates imply (Newmont -2.0% against -2.3%, Hecla -2.2% against -3.3%). Treasuries rose at the same time (the 10-year yield -6 bp, CNBC via StockTitan).
themes.mechanism: Through the miners' tie to the metal: their moves match what a year of daily returns implies from gold's fall.
themes.name: Gold fell with stocks instead of against them
themes.watch: Gold recovering while stocks keep falling would weaken the selling-winners reading; gold falling further with yields falling would fit it.

themes.beneath: BJ's settled its credit-card fee lawsuit in the quarter, which cut its selling and administrative costs by about $240 million before about $95 million of new costs (StockTitan, from its release); its adjusted EPS equals its reported $1.73, so the settlement is inside the beat. My inference: the market is pricing the 4.1% sales growth without gasoline and taking the beat as one-time.
themes.cause: BJ's beat and raised but is -6.1%: comparable club sales +13.5%, +4.1% without gasoline, EPS $1.73 against a $1.26 consensus (its 8-K; Investing.com). Natural Grocers is -9.8%: fourth-quarter sales +3.4% but EPS lower, on shrink, freight and new-store costs, and a fiscal 2027 EPS outlook from flat to modestly higher (its 8-K; MarketBeat on its call). Ross -5.0% and Gap +3.5% at about 8 a.m. ET (StockTitan).
themes.mechanism: Each on its own report; BJ's partners Kroger (+2.0%) and Costco (+1.4%) are up, so BJ's fall is its own.
themes.name: Retail reports: beats that do not hold up
themes.watch: BJ's call and the regular session: whether the fall holds once the settlement's size is spelled out.
